newsitem.title: THAILAND: Bank of Thailand says interest rates could ease.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Thailand says interest rates could ease.

text.p: Bank of Thailand Governor Rerngchai Marakanond said on Friday there were possibilities for current high domestic interest rates to ease as interbank rates in the money market were now more stable.
But the governor declined to speculate on when the easing of interest rates could start.

Thailand has some of the highest rates in the region with the minimum lending rate averaging around 13.25 percent. The central bank has maintained high rates, mainly to defend the baht against speculative attack from offshore players.
"The current interest rate reflects the cost of funds. However, it could be lower," Rerngchai said.

"I had discussions with the Thai Bankers Association earlier. They said if the interbank rate can be kept below 10 percent for a month, there would be room for the interest rates to come down," he said.
Overnight interbank rates have steadied to an average of around eight percent since the beginning of April after fluctuating upward sharply when the financial sector was in turmoil in March.
